text: Small Business Owner

Laguna Beach is home. My family put down roots here in the late 1940s, and I am proud to be a fourth-generation local. I attended Anneliese, El Morro, Thurston, and Laguna Beach High School, and I grew up on our beaches. My career in business and operations, managing teams and budgets worldwide, taught me practical, results-focused problem solving. I believe every generation has a responsibility to help steward its hometown, and I am ready to do my part.

Laguna is at a crossroads. Too many residents feel decisions are made without them. I have spent the past year at council meetings, town halls and listening to neighbors. The message is clear: residents want to be heard.

As your Council member, I will put residents first, with honest communication and real public input. Protect Laguna's small-town character, heritage, beaches, trees, and open space. Exercise fiscal discipline, prioritizing public safety, infrastructure, and core services over vanity projects and new taxes. Strengthen beach management and enforcement to address over-tourism. Support the businesses, artists, workers, and families who keep Laguna thriving year-round.
We only get one chance to be stewards of Laguna Beach. From Laguna, For Laguna.
Nickforlaguna.com

text: Retired Business Entrepreneur
Laguna Beach has been my home for more than 30 years. During that time, I have been committed to serving our community through business leadership, public service, and civic involvement.

My career has included executive leadership in the energy, communications, and technology industries, where I gained experience in strategic planning, responsible budgeting, and organizational leadership. I have also been honored to serve through appointments to the California New Motor Vehicle Board, the California Housing Finance Agency Board of Directors, and the Nevada-California High Speed Rail Board. Locally, I have proudly served as a Trustee and Board Member of the Laguna Art Museum.

I am running for City Council because I believe Laguna Beach deserves experienced, independent leadership that values transparency, fiscal responsibility, public safety, emergency preparedness, environmental stewardship, and thoughtful planning. Our city is unique, and I am committed to preserving its character while ensuring it remains financially strong, environmentally responsible, and an exceptional place to live, work, and visit.
Together, we can preserve what makes Laguna Beach extraordinary while planning responsibly for its future. I would be honored to earn your trust, your support, and your vote.

text: Small Business Owner

The Laguna Beach city council is under increasing pressure to approve questionable development projects, even in areas where it is prohibited, even if it means breaking our planning and environmental rules. I will resist that pressure.

Since moving here almost 30 years ago, I have worked tirelessly to protect our environment. That includes taking legal action when our council greenlights encroachment of development into our iconic hillsides and precious watercourses.

Our town is attracting ever more tourists and the council is investing the revenue to bring in even more people. I will work to redirect some of those funds toward critical resident needs such as sewer, water, and public safety infrastructure that has been neglected.

As a successful small business owner and developer who understands the importance of community buy-in, long-term planning, and fiscal discipline, I will ensure that our city’s budget is balanced without relying on out-of-scale developments and unchecked growth to pay our bills.

Laguna Beach is at a vital crossroad. Our town’s unique character, natural beauty, and financial stability are at stake. It’s time to put residents first, uphold our rules, and protect the Laguna we love. I ask for your vote.

text: Local Business Owner

For nearly two decades, I've led large, multi-department operations, managed complex budgets, created jobs, and built businesses by bringing people together to solve difficult problems. Choosing to open Oto Sushi in Laguna Beach wasn't just a business decision; it was a commitment to this community and its future.

I'm running for City Council because I believe Laguna Beach deserves leadership that asks the right questions, listens to the community, and plans for the future. My experience has taught me that the best decisions come from understanding the full picture, weighing tradeoffs, and focusing on long-term results, not short-term reactions.

My priorities are fiscal responsibility, public safety with a strong focus on wildfire preparedness, and building a strong local economy while preserving the character that makes Laguna Beach so special.

Whether you've lived here for decades or are new to Laguna, whether you're raising a family, building a career, running a business, creating art, or enjoying retirement, you deserve to have your voice heard. You deserve a City Council that listens before it decides, asks the right questions, and plans for the future. That's the change in leadership I will bring to Laguna Beach.

text: Laguna Beach City Councilmember

During my time on the Council, I have done my best to be thoughtful, open-minded, and effective. I’ve worked alongside a leadership team for whom I have enormous respect. We are not afraid to differ, and have used our differences to make better decisions for our community. And that’s how we will find good answers to hard questions. How can we keep our life-saving emergency room? Can we meet Sacramento's drastic housing mandates without sacrificing our autonomy? Can we further ramp up our efforts to police visitors who disregard the “house rules”. And, in an increasingly tough economy, can we live within our means more efficiently so that we can protect everything that makes Laguna Beach so unique? We continue to invest heavily in fire safety, implemented a stewardship plan to address visitor impacts like our Clean Laguna program, drone policing and a ban on canopies, and planned for local control of water availability with the addition of a new groundwater well in partnership with Newport Beach. These daunting challenges require the kind of collaborative work I love doing and — with your support and trust — pledge to continue doing for the hometown we love.

text: Urban Planning Entrepreneur
Development can move forward while protecting neighborhoods, quality of life, and the environment if we simply follow the rules.

My graduate education is in Urban and Regional Planning. For more than thirty years, I have led planning and policy efforts across California, including coastal development, while balancing environmental protection, property rights, public access, neighborhood concerns, and economic needs.
Since moving to Laguna Beach in 1986, my service has included working with the Open Space Committee, Affordable Housing Task Force, and Housing and Human Services Committee.

As your Councilmember, my priority will be to listen to you and your concerns before making a decision. My decisions will weigh neighborhood, environmental, and economic impacts to avoid disputes and reduce delays.

Our taxpayer dollars are precious. Even a city famous for sunshine needs a rainy-day fund. I will scrutinize the present and future cost of every major project and take into account what may go unfunded because of it.

Laguna needs to find the best way to balance public safety and infrastructure while supporting local businesses and protecting our hillsides, trees, ocean, beaches, and the character that makes Laguna Beach home. These will be my priorities.
I respectfully ask for your vote.

text: City Council Member, Laguna Beach

For generations, the people of Laguna Beach have shaped this extraordinary community through thoughtful decisions that protected its coast, unique neighborhoods, vibrant arts community, and natural beauty. Those choices created the Laguna Beach we enjoy today.

Working collaboratively with my City Council colleagues, we’ve strengthened wildfire preparedness, improved long-term water reliability, maintained one of California’s safest communities, and made City government more efficient and fiscally responsible.

My focus has always been Laguna Beach. I’ve worked to build on our community’s tradition of stewardship by bringing people together around a simple belief: our culture, heritage, and environment are interconnected, and our best decisions strengthen all three. That approach has helped support our arts community, protect our natural environment, strengthen our neighborhoods, and solve complex challenges with civility and respect.

Serving Laguna Beach has been one of the greatest honors of my life. I respectfully ask for your support so together we can continue protecting what makes Laguna Beach extraordinary while thoughtfully preparing for the opportunities and challenges of the next generation.

text: City Treasurer/CPA
As your elected City Treasurer, I have worked to protect Laguna Beach taxpayers and ensure that our city’s finances are managed responsibly, transparently, and with long-term fiscal discipline.
As a CPA and experienced financial professional, I understand the importance of careful budgeting, responsible investment of public funds, and accountability to our residents.

I am running for City Council to bring that same commitment, sound financial management, responsible spending, and protecting Laguna Beach’s unique character and quality of life. I will listen to residents, work collaboratively, and make decisions based on what is best for the long-term future of our community.
I respectfully ask for your vote and opportunity to continue serving Laguna Beach.

text: Laguna Beach City Councilmember
As a lifelong resident, I'm honored to serve the town three generations of my family call home. Laguna Beach is the product of visionaries who planned boldly for the future.

Public safety is our highest priority. As Mayor during the Rancho Fire, I witnessed our City at its best: prepared, coordinated, and resilient. Our investments in wildfire preparedness paid off. We fully funded our police; Laguna Beach has the lowest violent crime among Orange County beach cities.

Together, we’ve embraced long-term stewardship of our infrastructure and finances. Last year, I negotiated a historic agreement transitioning Laguna Beach from 100% imported water toward a majority-local supply. We cut permit times by nearly 30% and launched efficiency initiatives resulting in over $1.5 million in cuts.

The next four years will shape our next century. If re-elected, I will continue to lead the effort to retain an Emergency Room; expand our state-of-the-art wildfire defenses; implement a water resources strategy to strengthen resiliency and protect our ocean from sewer spills; and enhance our artistic culture with year-round live music at the Irvine Bowl.
There is no place like Laguna Beach. We inherited something extraordinary; our job is to leave it even stronger.
I respectfully ask for your vote.
alexforlaguna.com
